text:
Tessa Reed: hey all, accepted the GitHub invite to tessa@redwood.com but the SSO flow failed with a WebAuthn prompt for my YubiKey and then said 'Authorization denied'. I didn't get a keyboard prompt and now the org shows as pending. anyone seen yubikey+SSO fail like this? :cry:

Ben Li: welcome Tessa! yes, sometimes the browser will open the native WebAuthn dialog but if you have multiple security keys or a browser extension interfering it can silently fail. Which browser did you use?

Tessa Reed: Chrome on macOS. I tapped the key when it asked but the page immediately showed 'Authorization denied' and the banner on the repo said 'SAML SSO: Authorization required'.

Maya Franklin: Hi Tessa  quick checklist we use: 1) Accept invite on desktop, 2) when SSO prompts for WebAuthn pick the correct yubikey (some USB-C keys need an adapter), 3) if it fails, try Safari/Firefox as they surface the device prompt differently.

Tessa Reed: tried Safari and it actually asked to "Select a security device" and I picked the YubiKey, but then GitHub redirected to an error page mentioning "relying party not found".

DevOpsBot: Note: Our SSO provider requires that the browser origin match the allowed callback URLs. Some enterprise SSO redirects can be blocked by strict privacy extensions. Try disabling extensions or using an Incognito window with no extensions.

Ben Li: I can see a failed SSO attempt in the logs referencing Tessa's username tessa-reed. Maya, can you reissue the invite while I watch the org logs?

Maya Franklin: Re-sent invite to tessa@redwood.com and flagged it for SAML+WebAuthn. Tessa, accept in an Incognito window and when it prompts, touch the key and allow the browser prompt. If it still errors, reply here and we'll do a manual mapping.

Tessa Reed: Accepted in Incognito on Firefox and the SSO flow completed. It asked me to approve the app and register the security key as my second factor. Now GitHub shows me as a member but when I try to access repo infra-secrets I see "Request access" and a note that CODEOWNERS requires security-team approval. :thinking:

Ben Li: That makes senseour infra-secrets repo is gated by a CODEOWNERS policy requiring infra-security or security-reviewers. New hires don't get auto-membership in security teams. Which repos do you need immediate access to?

Tessa Reed: I need infra-secrets (read) and infra-deploy (write) for onboarding tasks. Also trying to push my dotfiles but git push gives 403. I suspect credential cache problems too.

Maya Franklin: I'll add you to infra-deploy via the devops team which grants write. For infra-secrets we require a security review ticket. People-ops will create the access request workflow (short form) and the security leads will triage. @people-ops can you start the security access ticket for Tessa?

people-ops: Opening a security access request now for infra-secrets (request-1835554321). Tessa, please confirm you completed SSO and registered your YubiKey so we can attach the SSO proof to the ticket. Also Ben: adding Tessa to teams devops and infra-deploy now.

Ben Li: Added to teams: devops, infra-deploy. You should have write to infra-deploy. infra-secrets will require sign-off. About the git 403: run `git remote -v` and check if origin is HTTPS. If so, clear credential helper entries or use `gh auth login`.

Tessa Reed: `git remote -v` shows HTTPS. I cleared macOS Keychain entries for github.com but `git push` still failed once until I ran `gh auth login --web` and authenticated with my work account. After that push succeeded.

Maya Franklin: Good. For others: WebAuthn can be finicky if you use a hardware key with multiple profiles or have enterprise policies. Best practice for onboarding: accept invites in an Incognito/Private window with extensions off, have YubiKey plugged in (or use platform authenticator), and run `gh auth login` after SSO to ensure CLI/credential helper tokens are linked to the work account.

people-ops: Security ticket opened and assigned to @security-leads. ETA for review ~24h. Once approved you'll get explicit repo access to infra-secrets. Meanwhile you have write on infra-deploy. Welcome aboard Tessa! :tada:

Tessa Reed: thanks all appreciate the quick help and the ticket. One small note: the onboarding doc doesn't mention YubiKey-specific steps; maybe we can add a short note about accepting invites in incognito and what to do if WebAuthn errors. Saved me a round-trip.

Ben Li: great suggestion I'll add a short troubleshooting blurb to the onboarding checklist about WebAuthn/YubiKey, and call out `gh auth login` after SSO.

DevOpsBot: If any other new hires hit WebAuthn issues during SSO, DM people-ops with your GitHub username and whether you used a security key; we'll reissue and assist.

Tessa Reed: all set for now. Thanks everyone :wave:
